question: Which of the following actions does insulin exert on liver tissue?

options.opa: It inhibits the uptake of glucose.
options.opc: Inhibits the synthesis of fatty acids.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "promotes glucose uptake in liver" -> "increased glycogen synthesis" -> "decreased blood glucose levels" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "inhibits glycogenolysis" -> "reduces glucose release from liver" -> "maintains lower blood glucose levels" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "activates glycogen synthase" -> "increases glycogen storage" -> "decreased blood glucose" -> 92%
CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "inhibits lipolysis" -> "reduces fatty acid release" -> "promotes fat storage" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "inhibits fatty acid synthesis" -> "possible unclear effect on fatty acid synthesis" -> "lower confidence" -> 70%
analysis: Insulin primarily promotes the storage of glucose in the liver by activating glycogen synthesis. It does not inhibit glucose uptake; rather, it facilitates it. Insulin also inhibits lipolysis and glycogenolysis, while promoting fatty acid synthesis. Therefore, the correct action of insulin on liver tissue is to activate glycogen synthesis.
